Hi Rebecca — thanks again for your time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery + demo and the recommended next steps for the model-fit evaluation we discussed. TL;DR: initial fit looks promising for clinical summarization and triage; recommended evaluation artifacts attached and links below.

What we observed on the call
- Primary need: extract structured problem/priority flags from intake notes and produce short clinician-facing summaries (<= 3 sentences).
- Data profile: average note length ~420 tokens, 95th percentile ~1,200 tokens, mix of templates + freeform.
- Quality concern: high false-positive triage flags are risk-critical — we recommended regression checks against your annotated set.

Redwood recommendations (shortlist)
1) Llama-3-70B-Chat (quantized) — best quality baseline for longer contexts; expect 95th latency percentile ~420 ms at 8 TPS (verified on our m60p pool).
2) RedWood-Optim-16B — lower cost / similar F1 on your triage labels in our initial tests; 95th latency ~180 ms at 20 TPS.
3) Falcon-40B-Instruct (sharded) — good balance for batch-heavy nightly runs (throughput 40 TPS in our bench).

Attached artifacts
- aperture_benchmark_report_v1.pdf (summary of throughput/latency percentiles, token counts, and accuracy on your sample set)
- prompt-pack-aperture-v1.json (seed prompts + eval prompt sets we ran)
- redwood_perf_profiles_aperture.csv (Redwood-verified latency/TPS profile per model variant)

Important notes on performance numbers
- Latency percentiles are measured on our Dedicated m60p configuration with continuous batching enabled; they are representative but will vary by private/hardware configs.
- TPS numbers are sustainable throughput under our steady-state eval harness (no cold-starts).

Suggested next steps (action items)
- Rebecca: share a 200–500 example gold set (PII redacted) we can run a targeted regression — goal: quantify false-positive reduction per model and per prompt variant.
- Dev: schedule a 2-hour deep-dive bench with Aperture's sample data (Dev to propose time windows).
- Marissa: prepare a short cost/latency tradeoff slide for the execs (we can reuse our perf CSV).

Links to run yourself
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ApertureBenchmarks
- Redwood perf profile viewer: https://redwood.example.com/perf/profiles/APTR-2026-087
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/APTR-2026-087

I attached the files referenced above. If you prefer, we can also run a smoke test on a small subset next week and share raw logs + KV cache behavior to validate burst latency.

Thanks — look forward to your sample.

Hi Rebecca — happy to map the numbers. Brief note below and I'll attach a short mapping doc to the Drive folder this morning.

Short mapping guidance
- Redwood numbers above were run on NVIDIA m60p equivalent (A100-style); Graviton-based CPU front-ends + g5 GPUs will see approximately:
  * Llama-3-70B-Chat (quantized): +15–25% higher 95p latency vs m60p baseline on g5 (due to different kernel efficiencies), throughput similar once warmed.
  * RedWood-Optim-16B: +5–12% latency delta on g5 vs m60p; good cost wins.
  * Falcon-40B-Instruct: sharded setups show similar throughput but higher variance on 99p latency under cold caches.

Guardrails for triage thresholds
- Start conservative: set triage trigger at model confidence >= 0.85 and require a 2x-weighted review for phrases containing keywords ("sepsis", "fall risk", "unstable vitals"). Use a small weekly sampling (n=50) to tune thresholds before broad rollout.

Attachments I'm adding to Drive now
- g5_mapping_note_APTR.pdf (short mapping guidance + config flags)
- smoke_test_playbook.md (how we'll run the 100-note smoke test and collect percentiles/cold-start logs)

I'll ping when the files are live.
